name: Gaolegao (高乐高, Cola Cao)
blurb: Spain's Cola Cao cocoa powder in China, a 1990s breakfast drink mixed into milk
title: What Is Gaolegao (高乐高)? Cola Cao in 1990s China
description: Gaolegao (高乐高) is the Chinese name of Spain's Cola Cao cocoa powder. Made in Tianjin from about 1990, it was a heavily advertised 1990s kids' drink.
answer: Gaolegao is the Chinese name of Cola Cao, a Spanish chocolate drink powder from Barcelona's Nutrexpa, which set up a joint venture in Tianjin around 1990. Stirred into milk, it was a heavily advertised and fairly pricey kids' drink in 1990s China, sold on the idea of healthy growth. Its China business was bought by the Philippine snack company Liwayway around 2015, after which advertising stopped and it faded, though the brand was never withdrawn.

body: Cola Cao was created in Barcelona in the mid-1940s and is still one of Spain's best-known cocoa powders. In China it became Gaolegao, a name that sounds like "high, happy, high", and many parents linked the "high" to growing tall.

It came in a tin and was meant to be mixed into milk, at a time when milk at breakfast was still new for many Chinese families. Besides cocoa, the China range added strawberry, banana and peach flavours, with a cartoon mascot team representing cocoa, calcium and zinc. Promotional gifts included stirring sticks and shaker cups, and Gaolegao-branded roll cakes were popular too.

head: Year
What happened
rows: Nutrexpa opens a Tianjin joint venture, reported as the first Spanish food company in China (some sources say 1988 or 1989)
A tin reportedly cost 30 to 50 yuan, when pork was 4 to 5 yuan a jin (500 g)
Official nutrition product of China's Atlanta Olympics delegation
Nutrition sponsor of China's gymnastics team at the Beijing Olympics
Liwayway buys the China business, reportedly for about US$13 million
Advertising stops, retail reach shrinks, the Tianjin plant closes in favour of contract making

body: Coverage in Chinese business media points to a few causes: it was always expensive, competition from milk drinks and imported cocoa grew, and after the sale it stopped advertising and missed the shift to e-commerce and livestream selling.

It still exists. A 2022 report noted Gaolegao could still be found on some supermarket shelves, and it kept an online store, but it is a shadow of its 1990s presence. In Spain, Cola Cao (now owned by Idilia Foods, formerly Nutrexpa) is sold as normal.

ul: Cartoon ads during children's programmes on CCTV
Stirring for ages to get the powder to dissolve
Being told it would make you grow taller
It cost more than the orange drink powder Tang (菓珍)

faq.q: Is Gaolegao the same as Cola Cao?
faq.a: Yes. Gaolegao is the Chinese name for Spain's Cola Cao cocoa powder.
The China business was bought by Liwayway, the Philippine maker of Oishi snacks, around 2015. Idilia Foods owns Cola Cao in Spain.

faq.q: Do you mix Gaolegao with water or milk?
faq.a: Milk. It is a cocoa drink powder designed to be stirred into milk.
